subject: Next steps: retriever sweep, reranker choice & regression gating for RAG pilot
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@medivault.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed RAG eval sweep (scope & quick asks)

Hi Hannah — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can kick off a lightweight qualification run: 

Recap (one-liner): Medivault wants a RAG pilot that (1) keeps hallucination <= 3% on the customer FAQ + regulatory doc set, (2) returns policies with traceable citations, and (3) meets a 400ms tail latency target for single-request lookups.

Proposed evaluation sweep (what Redwood will run):
- Retriever variants: BM25 baseline (index + lexical), Dense retriever (Faiss HNSW) with DPR embeddings, and a hybrid (lexical fallback).
- Retriever windows: top-50, top-200, top-500 (we'll measure recall@k and retrieval latency distribution).
- Rerankers: lightweight dual-encoder scoring vs cross-encoder (DistilBERT cross-encoder) for top-20 re-ranking experiments.
- Grounding metrics: hallucination rate (human-labeled at sample level), citation precision, answer faithfulness score, MRR@10, recall@50.
- Prompt sets: we will run your provided customer prompts plus our curated prompt-suite_v3 (attached).

Quick asks from you to start the sweep: 
1) A short sample corpus (500–2k docs) or a Drive link to representative docs you’re comfortable using for an initial test.
2) Confirmation of any blacklisted doc types (PII, legal hold).
3) If we need to include any internal denial language or special citation formats.

Deliverables: initial benchmark report (CSV + short executive summary) + a Jupyter notebook with plots; target turnaround 3 business days from receiving the sample corpus.

I attached the prompt suite and a short delta doc for retriever configs. Ben and Monica — flagged you for the reranker trade-offs and to coordinate staffing for the human-labeling pass.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: prompt_suite_v3.jsonl (JSONL)]

From: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@medivault.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medivault Engineering <eng@medivault.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed RAG eval sweep (scope & quick asks)

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear recap. All sounds good; a couple of clarifications before you start: 

1) Corpus: here's a drive folder with a 1,200-doc sample set (policies, FAQs, product spec excerpts): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/medivault-sample-1200 (please keep access internal).
2) Blacklist: anything marked "LegalHold" in metadata should be excluded.
3) Citation format: we prefer inline citations with doc id + page range when available (e.g., [DOC-271, p.3]).

On hallucination gating: the 3% target is on the human-evaluated sample set; if any config exceeds 6% we will require a regression gating discussion.

Also: can you include a quick A/B on quantized vs fp16 serving for the dense retriever path? We want to understand if 8-bit quantization materially shifts hallucination or citation fidelity.

—Hannah
Hannah Lowe
Head of Product — Knowledge & Search | Medivault
[Attachment: medivault-sample-access.txt (link stub)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Lowe <hannah.lowe@medivault.com>
Date: 2027-09-22T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed RAG eval sweep (scope & quick asks)

Copying the plan into an ops checklist and answering Hannah's asks. Short notes and recommendations from an ops/accuracy perspective: 

- Retriever window sanity: top-200 is usually the sweet spot for short-doc corpora (<= 2k docs) — top-50 can miss context for multi-paragraph policies, top-500 often adds noise and increases hallucination if reranker precision is low. We'll measure recall@50/200/500 and compare.
- Reranker tradeoffs: dual-encoder (fast) for production throughput; cross-encoder (slower) for accuracy. For the pilot we recommend cross-encoder for the benchmark (to measure best-case grounding) and a parallel experiment with a distilled cross-encoder for a production-like latency point.
- Quantization: we will test both fp16 and 8-bit quantized kernels for the dense retriever + reranker stack. Hypothesis: quantization can slightly increase hallucination via score perturbation; we'll flag any config that shows >1.5x hallucination vs fp16.
- Human-labeling plan: Monica — can we stand up a 400-sample labeling pass (binary hallucination + citation correctness)? We can use a stratified sample across low/med/high confidence answers.

Operational next steps (owners + dates):
1) Sofia — confirm Drive link access and sign-off on exclusion list (today EOD).
2) Ben — spin up benchmark run (top-50/200/500 x retrievers x rerankers x quant modes) and return initial CSV (target: 72 hours).
3) Monica — recruit labeling pool and provide labeling guide (target: 48 hours).
4) Sofia + Hannah — plan a 30-minute readout once we have initial CSV (tentative: 2027-09-27).

I'll attach the config delta and a template CSV for results.

Ben Carter
Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: retriever_config_deltas.md (MD)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — quick status update and final confirmations: 

- Access: Hannah — I have Drive access to the "medivault-sample-1200" folder and verified LegalHold tags are present. Excluding those now.
- Labeling: Monica confirmed the 400-sample human-label pool; labeling guide attached.
- Benchmark kickoff: Ben has scheduled the sweep to start today (09/23) on a small dedicated pool — configuration combinations: [BM25, Dense(fp16), Dense(8-bit), Hybrid] x [rerank: dual-encoder, cross-encoder, distilled-cross] x [top-k: 50/200/500].

Deliverable cadence: initial CSV + executive summary by EOB Monday (09/27); full notebook and plots by Wednesday (09/29). If any config shows hallucination > 6% we'll pause that config and escalate to the gating group (SLA/contract implications noted).

Action items: 
- Hannah: confirm we can share a small anonymized sample of any labeled false positives back to your team for root cause analysis (yes/no by EOD).
- Ben: kick off run and paste the first S3/Drive link to results in this thread when ready.
- Monica: upload labeling guide + start labeler onboarding.

Thanks — will keep this thread as the source of truth for the pilot.

Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
